title: Tesla opens Cybercab orders at $29,990 plus $299 a month
h1: Tesla has opened Cybercab orders to select customers at $29,990, with a $299 monthly fee needed to make the car drive
description: Tesla began inviting select customers on November 13, 2026 to order a Cybercab for $29,990. It needs a $299 monthly subscription and works only in robotaxi zones.
standfirst: The two-seat car has no steering wheel or pedals, so it only runs inside the areas where Tesla already operates its robotaxi service. Federal regulators have not yet ruled on whether it meets safety standards.
keywords: Tesla Cybercab order, Cybercab price, Cybercab $299 subscription, Tesla Autonomy Subscription, Cybercab geofence, Tesla robotaxi cities, Cybercab NHTSA
takeaways: Tesla invited select customers on Friday, November 13, 2026 to order a Cybercab for personal use at $29,990 before taxes.
The car needs a $299 monthly subscription to operate, about $3,588 a year, and the order takes a $1,000 non-refundable deposit.
Estimated delivery is December 2026, and the car works only inside Tesla's robotaxi service areas.
body: Tesla has started taking orders for the Cybercab, its two-seat car with no steering wheel or pedals. The company said Friday evening, November 13, that select customers could order one for personal use, TechCrunch reported. The price is $29,990, and the estimated delivery date is December 2026.

The purchase price is only part of the bill. The car will not move unless the owner also pays $299 a month for what Tesla calls an Autonomy Subscription, according to Electrek, which reviewed the order page. That works out to $3,588 a year. The order includes one month of the subscription and requires a $1,000 non-refundable deposit.
CEO Elon Musk called the monthly fee too high and said it should be closer to what other Tesla owners pay for Full Self-Driving and connectivity, roughly $115 a month, TechCrunch reported.

Only inside the areas where Tesla already runs its robotaxi service. Electrek lists eight cities: Austin, Dallas, Houston, Fort Worth and San Antonio in Texas, and Miami, Orlando and Tampa in Florida. It reported that delivery is set for Austin. TechCrunch, citing tech reviewer Marques Brownlee, said buyers must take delivery in one of a handful of Texas cities. Musk said the car will be sold nationwide as Tesla gets regulatory approval.

A federal safety question is still open. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration ordered Tesla to show how a car with no brake pedal meets federal standards that require one, Electrek reported. Tesla replied on October 30 and asked that its answer be kept confidential. The agency has not ruled.
The Cybercab is central to Tesla's plans. The company intends to end Cybertruck production next year and use that factory space to build more Cybercabs.
